items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...seems like the mainstream tradition that’s being carried on in jazz today is mostly the white musicians — Ken Peplowski and Randy — [INTERVIEWEE] Oh yes it’s certainly true.

ctx.x: Savoy Ballroom began to bring in white bands. In any event, it has reached the point where today there are very, very fine white musicians who can’t really find work and that especially holds in Europe where there was always a feeling of the, what shall we say, the romance and I don’t know the word exactly, the glamour of the primitive black man and his primitive music. That’s the way the early jazz fans seemed to look at jazz. And once that got washed away and people realized well that’s an inaccurate…
From what I see, and please correct me if I’m wrong, it seems like the mainstream tradition that’s being carried on in jazz today is mostly the white musicians — Ken Peplowski and Randy —

Oh yes it’s certainly true. But there’s a reason for it, which is a very unfortunate one. And that is that the younger white musicians don’t know the foundation of what they consider their music. They simply don’t go into it and—
